findings.title: Version/release manifest-object publish and backfill will crash on the ~25k library-snapshot corpus because StandardVersion.checksum / TerminologyRelease.checksum is a synthetic group digest, not a file sha256
findings.where: Decision 3 (manifest-file publish), Decision 5 (publish-assets verify_repository_asset on version/release rows), Exact files items 6 and 7
findings.detail: register_library_snapshot sets StandardVersion/TerminologyRelease.checksum = _group_checksum(resources), a synthetic digest over the group inventory with no corresponding on-disk file. checksum_object_key(version.checksum) points at a nonexistent object and verify_repository_asset(version.asset_path, version.checksum) raises 'repository asset checksum mismatch' for every library-snapshot version/release row, breaking the inline publish and the resumable backfill. No read path keys off the version/release checksum, so the object is both impossible to produce for the bulk path and unnecessary.
findings.fix: Publish only objects whose checksum is a real file sha256: per-asset StandardAsset/TerminologyAsset rows (item.sha256) plus, on the hand-maintained importer paths only, the manifest file (whose sha256 equals the stored version/release checksum there). In publish-assets, skip or treat-as-no-own-object the standard_versions/terminology_releases rows whose stored checksum is a group digest. Stop asserting the version/release checksum is a universal file checksum.

findings.title: Terminology importer publish instruction references manifest.assets and per-asset TerminologyAsset rows that this path never creates
findings.where: Decision 3 'What the publish pass must cover (Finding 4)', Exact files item 7
findings.detail: import_terminology_manifest creates only TerminologyRelease/Codelist/Term rows and the CT manifest has no assets collection; TerminologyAsset rows exist only on the library-snapshot path. The 'publish every per-asset terminology row' rule is inapplicable to the hand-maintained CT importer and misleads the implementer.
findings.fix: Scope the publish rule per path: hand-maintained standards importer publishes each StandardAsset + manifest file; hand-maintained terminology importer publishes the manifest file only; library snapshot publishes each StandardAsset/TerminologyAsset (item.sha256) with the version/release row having no own file object.

findings.title: catalog_seed 'publish at each session.add site' is ambiguous about the idempotency guard, determining whether a DB-exists/object-missing state self-heals
findings.where: Decision 3 '_checksum stays pure (Finding 6)', Exact files item 5
findings.detail: Each seed session.add is nested in an 'if session.get(...) is None:' guard. If publish is inside the guard, a DB that has the rows but is missing the objects (the migration target case) will skip publishing silently; if outside, re-seed re-publishes harmlessly. The design does not say which.
findings.fix: Publish outside/before the 'if session.get(...) is None' guard using the resolved path and _checksum(path), so seed() is self-healing for DB-exists/object-missing and an idempotent no-op otherwise; keep the single terminal commit.

findings.title: object_missing and storage_error collapse to the same 503 code asset_content_unavailable, defeating the distinction Decision 0 insists on
findings.detail: Decision 0 exists specifically to tell object_missing apart from storage_error without parsing messages, but the HTTP mapping emits one code for both, so clients/operators cannot distinguish 'run publish-assets' (deployment state) from 'object storage is down' (transient infra).
findings.fix: Give distinct stable codes while keeping 503: object_missing -> asset_content_unpublished, storage_error -> asset_content_store_unavailable. Update the table, contract-test assertions, and Open-ambiguities item 8.

findings.title: 'established sibling-route pattern' for request.app.state.settings is overstated for catalogs.py
findings.detail: request.app.state.settings is a real platform pattern (artifacts/integration routes) and app.state.settings is set in create_app, but it is not currently used in catalogs.py; the content handlers take neither Request nor storage today.
findings.fix: Reword to 'the established platform pattern (artifacts/integration routes)' and note both content handlers must newly add request: Request and the get_object_storage dependency.

findings.title: load_presentation_template missing-row error is a bare RuntimeError, described imprecisely and as if part of the Decision 6 problem mapping
findings.detail: Actual raise is RuntimeError('validated Template version is missing') (not 'template version is missing'), a bare RuntimeError not a ProblemException. In the phase split it moves to the worker-phase build_artifact_payload, so it is not a request-path typed problem.
findings.fix: Quote the error text accurately and state it stays a worker-phase RuntimeError unchanged, outside the content-error HTTP mapping which covers only AssetContentError from the byte read.
